members.title: Sheikh Hasina’s wish to return home on 16 Dec is different from reality: Humaiun Kobir
members.lead: Foreign Affairs State Minister Humaiun Kobir has said that Sheikh Hasina’s wish to return home on 16 December is different from reality. If she is to return, she will have to come as a prisoner, wearing handcuffs. Humaiun Kobir made the comment today, Tuesday morning, in response to questions from journalists after a briefing for foreign diplomats at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The state minister for foreign affairs said the foreign diplomats had been informed at today’s briefing that the people of Bangladesh were taking a tough stance against Awami League terrorists. The government’s position was presented to the diplomats in the context of recent violence and acts of sabotage in the country, he added. . Sources at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the briefing stated that, following the 2024 mass uprising, the BNP formed the government under the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman after a free and fair election on 12 February 2026. The new government began working to strengthen democratic institutions, restore law and order, and bring back economic stability. . However, leaders and activists of the Awami League (whose activities are currently banned in the country) and its affiliated organisations are carrying out violence and acts of sabotage across the country. The heads of around 60 missions, including those of the United States, the United Kingdom, India, China and Japan, as well as representatives of several international organisations, including the United Nations, attended the briefing.

members.title: It is rare to seek aircraft for fugitive accused: Chief Prosecutor
members.lead: International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) Chief Prosecutor Aminul Islam has described the wish of Sheikh Hasina, who has been sentenced to death for crimes against humanity, to return to Bangladesh on 16 December as a delusion. On this matter, he said that it was rare in the world for someone to request an aircraft on behalf of a fugitive accused. The chief prosecutor made these remarks in response to questions from journalists at the ICT today, Tuesday. . Deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina wants to return to Bangladesh on 16 December, Victory Day. She has called on the government to arrange for her return from Delhi, India, on an aircraft of Biman Bangladesh Airlines, the state-owned flag carrier. Sheikh Hasina’s spokesperson informed the Reuters news agency of this today, Tuesday. Asked about the matter, Aminul Islam said, “This is a ridiculous incident. The issue of requesting an aircraft—the spokesperson who made this demand—is nothing more than a delusion on his part. The reason is that it is rare in the world for someone to request an aircraft on behalf of a fugitive accused. Therefore, such a demand cannot be accepted under any circumstances.” A journalist asked whether the Bangladesh government had failed in its responsibility when people who were declared fugitives by the tribunal and are being tried in absentia were holding press conferences in Delhi and coming to the Bangladesh border areas, including Agartala and Petrapole. . In response, the chief prosecutor said, “They are not doing anything inside Bangladesh’s territory. Now, their activities are being seen in other countries through various media outlets.
